sentences.text: The Orionids are born from dust left by Halley's Comet on past returns; Earth crosses this trail every October.
Halley itself is now beyond the orbit of Neptune, slowly heading for its return in 2061.
Let us move in to Earth's orbit: the dust grains strike the atmosphere at sixty-six kilometres a second and leave long, bright trails.
At peak about twenty meteors an hour are seen; the radiant lies near the club raised by Orion the Hunter.
We meet the other half of the same dust trail in May as the Eta Aquariid shower.
